name: stri_count_regex
title: Count the Number of Pattern Occurrences

origin.description: Count how many times a regular expression matches each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Matches do not overlap. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
origin.value: An integer vector. A missing result is NA.
origin.example:
result <- stri_count_regex("bab baab baaab", "b.*?b")
cat(paste0('stri_count_regex("bab baab baaab", "b.*?b") returns ', result, '.\n'))

translation.description: Count how many times a regular expression matches each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Regular expression, missing value, or list of those. An empty pattern yields NA.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: None, or a dict of only the regex settings that were supplied.

translation.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Matches do not overlap. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive.
translation.value: A list of integers. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.regex import stri_count_regex
result = stri_count_regex("bab baab baaab", "b.*?b")
print(f'stri_count_regex("bab baab baaab", "b.*?b") returns {result[0]}.')
